results.title: Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA)
results.content: # Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA). * Inter-annotator Agreement (IAA) is a statistical measure that quantifies the consistency among human annotators using metrics such as Cohen’s κ and Krippendorff’s α. Inter-annotator Agreement (IAA) is the fundamental statistical and methodological construct quantifying consistency among human annotators engaged in labeling, segmenting, or otherwise providing structured judgments over datasets. * Routine reporting of both **inter-** and **intra-annotator agreement**; intra-annotator agreement tracks label stability over time and isolates causes of low IAA due to subjective variance versus ambiguity or guideline inadequacy (Abercrombie et al., 2023). **Worker reliability weighting**: By leveraging inter-annotator and intra-annotator agreement, frameworks such as EffiARA compute annotator reliability scores used to re-weight samples during model training, directly improving downstream classifier performance—especially in low-agreement or subjective tasks (Cook et al., 2024). * **Multi-faceted reporting:** Combine intra-annotator agreement with IAA to dissect stability versus reliability and employ diagnostic matrices that distinguish subjectivity from ambiguity (Abercrombie et al., 2023). 4.
